stories.title: Fund Administrator Hanover Park Inks 19K-SF Deal at 387 Park Avenue South
stories.excerpt: An artificial intelligence-driven fund administrator is moving its headquarters to TF Cornerstone’s 387 Park Avenue South, Commercial Observer has learned. Hanover Park signed a 19,269-square-foot lease on the entire 10th floor of the NoMad property, marking its fifth office move in two years, according to CEO Chris Hladczuk. The firm’s most recent office address is listed on its website as 115 East 23rd Street. TF Cornerstone did not immediately provide the asking rent or the length of the lease, but the average asking rent for office space in Midtown South was $85.73 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a report from CBRE. “Existing tenants are choosing to expand here and new companies are choosing to locate here,” Joe Lanzilotta, director of commercial asset management at TF Cornerstone, said in a statement. “The property continues to outperform the market as a destination for growing businesses.” It is unclear who represented the tenant in the transaction, but Cushman & Wakefield’s Ethan Silverstein handled negotiations on behalf of the landlord in the deal signed in July. It’s unclear who represented the tenant. “The combination of TF Cornerstone’s long-term investment, highly efficient 20,000-square-foot floor plates and premier NoMad location continues to resonate with tenants,” Silverstein said in a statement. “The recent leasing activity demonstrates that companies are prioritizing best-in-class buildings, and with one full floor becoming available this fall, the property remains well positioned to meet continued demand.” Other recent deals in the 230,000-square-foot building at the corner of Park Avenue South and East 27th Street include a lease for marketing firm PMG Worldwide, which expanded from the second to third floor in May and brought its total footprint there to 38,744 square feet, according to TF Cornerstone. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Hanover Park (AI fund admin) leases 19.3K SF at 387 Park Avenue South, NoMad Manhattan
Midtown South office asking rent averages $85.73/SF in Q2 2026; tenant expansion signals market traction
Fifth office move in two years indicates instability or rapid growth; lease terms not disclosed
stories.summary: Hanover Park, an AI-driven fund administrator, signed a 19,269-SF lease for the entire 10th floor at TF Cornerstone's 387 Park Avenue South in NoMad, its fifth office relocation in two years. Average asking rent in Midtown South was $85.73/SF in Q2 2026. TF Cornerstone management cited existing tenant expansions and new company relocations as evidence the property outperforms market benchmarks.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. Office leasing activity in Manhattan does not materially signal apartment demand or supply conditions; financial services tenants in NoMad do not anchor residential absorption. Monitor only if office-to-residential conversion becomes feasible on underutilized office assets in that submarket.

stories.title: Peachtree Recaps Ritz-Carlton Portland With $141M C-PACE Loan
stories.excerpt: A New York lender is more than ready for a Portland hospitality resurgence. Ready Capital, which assumed full ownership of the The Ritz-Carlton Portland mixed-use project following a foreclosure in July 2025, just secured $141 million of commercial property accessed clean energy (C-PACE) debt for the recapitalization of the 35-story tower, Commercial Observer has learned. Peachtree Group originated the C-PACE loan for the 2023-completed Block 216 Tower development that features a 251-key hotel, 131 condominium units and 159,000 square feet of office space. Construction of the Ritz-Carlton-Portland, the Marriott’s brand’s first hotel in the Pacific Northwest, commenced in 2019 before encountering delays due to the COVID-19 pandemic and ensuing struggles to the city’s economy. Jared Schlosser, head of credit originations at Peachtree Group, said condo units at the property have sold at a healthy pace and the hotel is well positioned for success as one of the newest lodging offerings in the Portland region. “It’s the nicest hotel up there and that pocket of Portland is revitalizing,” Schlosser told CO. “I think there’s probably more tailwinds ahead versus headwinds for Portland.” Schlosser added that C-PACE debt was conducive for the recap since as a newer building it was developed under “stringent” building codes with much of the project eligible for retroactive financing. He noted that the deal marks Peachtree’s second largest loan. Ready Capital set the stage for owning The Ritz-Carlton Portland when it acquired a prior construction loan on the development valued at more than $500 million through a 2022 merger with Mosaic Real Estate Investors. The lender manages the property in partnership with Lincoln Property Company. Ready Capital did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Ready Capital (foreclosed July 2025) refinances Ritz-Carlton Portland Block 216 with $141M C-PACE debt
Project contains 251-key hotel, 131 condos, 159K SF office; condo sales at healthy pace
C-PACE financing preserves mixed-use development; signals post-COVID recovery confidence in Portland hospitality
stories.summary: Ready Capital, which assumed ownership of the Ritz-Carlton Portland (Block 216 Tower) following foreclosure in July 2025, secured $141 million in C-PACE debt for recapitalization. The 35-story mixed-use project, completed in 2023, includes 251 hotel keys, 131 condominiums, and 159,000 SF of office space. Condo units are selling at a healthy pace, and the hotel is well-positioned as the Marriott brand's first property in the Pacific Northwest.
stories.impact: Portland multifamily development window narrowing as hotel-condo hybrid assets recycle through foreclosure and refinance. Mixed-use projects with residential components may face valuation pressure if debt markets tighten; C-PACE availability is critical to feasibility. Monitor Portland's condo absorption and pricing; strong condo sales suggest underlying demand that could support purpose-built rental development in adjacent sites.

stories.title: Office Furniture Manufacturer Haworth Renews 30K SF at SL Green’s 125 Park Avenue
stories.excerpt: Office furniture manufacturer Haworth is staying seated at 125 Park Avenue. Haworth has signed a 10-year lease renewal for its 30,365-square-foot office and showroom space at the 25-story Midtown office building, landlord SL Green Realty announced Wednesday. The company, which manufactures and sells high-end, ergonomic office seating and workspaces, has been a tenant in the property, also known as the Pershing Square Building, for more than a decade. The firm, which did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment, previously renewed its lease for the same space back in 2015, CO reported at the time. The asking rent was $100 per square foot. SL Green was represented in-house in this deal, while Haworth was represented by Ethan Silverstein and Amy Zhen from Cushman & Wakefield. C&W did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “We are proud to extend our valued relationship with Haworth at 125 Park Avenue,” Steven Durels, executive vice president and director of leasing and real property at SL Green, said in a statement. “The building’s proximity to Grand Central Terminal and our new lobby and elevator cab renovation have helped maintain 99 percent occupancy.” SL Green acquired 125 Park Avenue in 2010 for $330 million, according to property records. The building sits across the street from Grand Central Terminal on Park Avenue and East 42nd Street. Other tenants in the building include banking and investment firm TD Securities and real estate brokerage Newmark. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Haworth (office furniture mfr) renews 30.4K SF at SL Green's 125 Park Avenue for 10 years
Tenant occupies space 10+ years; previous renewal in 2015; Midtown location near Grand Central
Long-term office lease renewal signals occupant stability but no growth signal
stories.summary: Haworth, a high-end ergonomic office furniture manufacturer, renewed its 30,365-SF lease at SL Green's 125 Park Avenue (Pershing Square Building) for 10 years. Haworth has been a tenant for more than a decade and previously renewed the space in 2015. The 25-story Midtown building benefits from proximity to Grand Central Terminal.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Office lease renewals do not signal residential demand or supply shifts. Note only if SL Green or other major office REITs begin office-to-residential conversion strategies in Midtown Manhattan submarkets.

stories.title: CBRE Promotes Anna Wolke (Faktorow) and Stuart Dyer in the Firm’s Data Center Solutions Group
stories.excerpt: CBRE announced that Anna Wolke (Faktorow) and Stuart Dyer have been promoted to executive vice president within the firm’s Data Center Solutions Group. Based in Northern Virginia, Wolke and Dyer advise developers, investors, institutional owners and occupiers across the U.S. data center sector. Alongside their team, they have played a role in some of the industry’s most significant transactions. Collectively, Wolke, Dyer and team have completed more than $28 billion in capital markets transactions and 45 powered land transactions valued at more than $2.1 billion. “The explosive growth of cloud computing and digital infrastructure is reshaping the data center sector, creating both new opportunities and new complexity for our clients,” said Kyle Schoppmann, President, CBRE Mid-Atlantic. “Anna and Stu have been instrumental in helping clients navigate that growth while contributing to the continued expansion of our Data Center Solutions business.” Wolke specializes in advising data center developers, investors and institutional owners on capital markets and strategic real estate transactions. Dyer advises clients across the artificial intelligence, cloud and federal sectors on data center occupancy and development strategies. bullets: CBRE promotes Wolke and Dyer to EVP, Data Center Solutions Group based in Northern Virginia
Team has closed $28B+ in capital markets and 45 powered land deals ($2.1B+)
Data center growth reshaping infrastructure; no direct multifamily signal
stories.summary: CBRE announced promotions of Anna Wolke (Faktorow) and Stuart Dyer to executive vice president within the Data Center Solutions Group, based in Northern Virginia. The team and leadership have completed more than $28 billion in capital markets transactions and 45 powered land deals valued at $2.1 billion+. Growth reflects explosive expansion in cloud computing and digital infrastructure.
stories.impact: Indirect relevance: data center capital influx and land acquisition in Northern Virginia (Ashburn, Loudoun County corridor) may constrain developable land supply and drive land prices higher, compressing multifamily development feasibility in tier-one data center hubs. Monitor land values in data center-heavy submarkets; infrastructure investment does not inherently increase residential demand but can inflate real estate costs.

stories.title: CMBS Loan Backed by Vornado, Related’s 85 10th Avenue Sent to Special Servicing
stories.excerpt: A $396 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan secured by 85 10th Avenue, a 633,000-square-foot office property in Manhattan’s Chelsea neighborhood, has been sent to special servicing due to imminent maturity default, according to an alert from Morningstar Credit. 85 10th Avenue is owned jointly by Vornado Realty Trust and the Related Companies. Related purchased the property in 2007 from Somerset Partners for $430 million and brought Vornado in as a 50/50 partner. The $396 million loan makes up DBWF 2016-85T and is part of larger conduits CD 2017-CD3 and BACM 2017-BNK3. It is expected to default ahead of its December 2026 maturity date, according to Morningstar. The building’s largest tenant, Google, currently takes up 47 percent of its space, as the firm has gradually expanded since signing a 180,000-square-foot lease in 2014. But cash flow from rents has declined lately, particularly since the COVID-19 pandemic. Morningstar Credit reports that 85 10th Avenue’s cash flow fell 28 percent below underwriting in 2025, and that biometric screening company CLEAR, which signed a 120,000-square-foot lease for a new headquarters in 2021, is currently in a rent abatement period. Vornado reported that the building’s occupancy stood at 89 percent in its most recent second-quarter earnings supplemental. The 11-story 85 10th Avenue first opened in 1913 as a Nabisco factory and was redeveloped for commercial office use in the late 1990s. Vornado and Related invested into renovating the lobby in 2023. Vornado and Related did not respond to requests for comment. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: 85 10th Avenue (633K SF office, Vornado/Related JV) CMBS loan $396M sent to special servicing
Google tenant occupies 47% (180K SF lease from 2014); imminent maturity default expected Dec 2026
Office property distress signals ongoing Chelsea/Midtown office weakness post-COVID
stories.summary: A $396 million CMBS loan secured by 85 10th Avenue, a 633,000-SF office building in Manhattan's Chelsea owned jointly by Vornado and Related Companies, has been sent to special servicing due to imminent maturity default. Google is the largest tenant, occupying 47% of the property. The loan is expected to default ahead of its December 2026 maturity as cash flow has declined since the COVID-19 pandemic.
stories.impact: Manhattan office distress may accelerate conversion or redevelopment opportunities in Chelsea/Midtown South, but only if underlying economics support office-to-residential conversion. Vornado/Related distress does not directly signal multifamily demand; however, if Google's lease renewal or expansion falters, the property could become a conversion candidate. Monitor for sales or restructuring that might unlock development rights.

stories.title: Newgard Group Buys West Palm Dev Site to Build Car-Centric Private Club
stories.excerpt: Harvey Hernandez’s Newgard Group bought a development site in West Palm Beach, Fla., to build an upscale parking garage with a private members club component. The Miami-based developer paid $10.5 million for a 2.6-acre parcel at 2500 North Florida Mango Road, just north of Palm Beach International Airport, property records show. Called Palm Beach Auto Haus, the upcoming two-story development will be a private members club with space to park 20 cars and amenities that include padel courts, coworking lounges, a cafe and a gym. The project marks somewhat of a departure for a new-to-market developer in West Palm Beach, most of whom have launched luxury condo developments near the city’s waterfront. “For years I searched for a place that reflected the way passionate automobile enthusiasts truly enjoy their collections,” Hernandez, founder and CEO of Newgard Group, said in a statement. “We envisioned something far beyond traditional car storage — a destination centered around ownership, design, community and unforgettable experiences.” Newgard Group nabbed a $6.3 million acquisition loan from Belmont Bank & Trust. The seller, a Thousand Oaks, Calif.-based entity tied to Jonathan and Justin Bergman, had purchased the asset, which holds a 29,790-square-foot commercial building, for $3.5 million in 2021. The Bergmans could not be reached for comment. In Miami’s Brickell district, Newgard Group is building a waterfront, luxury condo complex alongside Two Roads Development, after securing a $513 million debt package last year. Earlier this month, it sold off a piece of land for $50 million to another development team. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Newgard Group buys 2.6-acre West Palm Beach site for $10.5M to build car-centric private club
Palm Beach Auto Haus: 20-car parking, padel courts, coworking, cafe, gym; non-residential use
Novel use case; minimal multifamily supply or demand signal
stories.summary: Newgard Group paid $10.5 million for a 2.6-acre development site at 2500 North Florida Mango Road in West Palm Beach, just north of Palm Beach International Airport. The developer will build Palm Beach Auto Haus, a two-story private members club featuring space for 20 cars, padel courts, coworking lounges, a cafe, and a gym. The project marks a departure from typical luxury waterfront condo developments in West Palm Beach.
stories.impact: No multifamily relevance. Specialty automotive/lifestyle club does not impact residential demand, supply, or market fundamentals in West Palm Beach.

stories.title: After 30-Year Hold, Monarch Offloads Golden Apartment Community
stories.excerpt: Monarch Investment & Management Group sold Fox Hill Apartments, a 153-unit garden-style community in Golden, Colorado for $32 million. Monarch Investment & Management Group owned Fox Hill for nearly 30 years. Sierra Parkway Communities was the buyer. JLL represented Monarch in the sale of the property. JLL Capital Market’s Sales and Advisory team was led by Jordan Robbins, Wick Kirby, Alex Possick and Seth Gallman. JLL asserts that the 1972-built property at 17611 W. 16th Ave. presents a value-add opportunity, with the ability to renovate 100% of its unit interiors to a standardized scope while enhancing outdoor amenity spaces. The average in-place rent of $1,645 sits significantly below the area’s $908,000 median home price, creating a 3.30-times premium to own versus rent within a one-mile radius. Current rent levels represent just 15% of average household incomes exceeding $128,000 in the immediate area. The property maintains 95% occupancy and has averaged 96% occupancy since 2021. The post After 30-Year Hold, Monarch Offloads Golden Apartment Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Monarch Investment sells Fox Hill Apartments (153 units, Golden, CO) after 30-year hold for $32M
1972-built property; in-place rent $1,645 vs. area median home $908K; 95% occupancy, 96% avg since 2021
Value-add candidate: rents only 15% of $128K+ household income; renovation upside apparent
stories.summary: Monarch Investment & Management Group sold Fox Hill Apartments, a 153-unit garden-style community in Golden, Colorado, to Sierra Parkway Communities for $32 million after a 30-year hold. The 1972-built property has in-place rent of $1,645 and maintains 95% occupancy. Rents represent only 15% of average household income ($128,000+) in the immediate area, creating significant value-add opportunity through unit renovations and amenity upgrades.
stories.impact: Golden, CO market signal: strong occupancy and below-market rents indicate underlevered asset and underlying demand resilience. Sierra Parkway acquisition suggests investor confidence in Denver metro rental fundamentals and renovation-driven value creation. Wide gap between rent-to-income ratio and comparable home prices signals opportunity for rent growth through operational improvements; monitor Golden/Denver vintage multifamily dispositions as pipeline indicator for value-add development.

stories.title: BH Adds Nearly 300K-SF Asset to Plano Office Portfolio
stories.excerpt: BH Properties completed the acquisition of Tollway North Office Park, a 297,591-square-foot, seven-building business park in Plano, Texas. The acquisition follows the firm’s February 2025 purchase of the adjacent R&D at Legacy campus, bringing BH’s ownership within the Legacy Business Park to more than 675,000 square feet across fourteen buildings. BH acquired the property from KBS. KBS was represented by Newmark’s Dallas team of Gary Carr, Chris Murphy, Robert Hill, and Austin Sheahan, while BH was represented by Scott Henry. Currently, approximately 70% leased, Tollway North consists of seven single-story office buildings totaling nearly 300,000 square feet and provides tangible value-add opportunities. Stream Realty’s Chase Lopez, James Mantzuranis, and Sam Bass in Dallas will be representing BH on leasing. The area is home to numerous Fortune 500 and global companies, with AT&T’s planned global headquarters expected to bring thousands of its employees to the immediate area beginning in 2028. Connect Texas Multifamily in Dallas on August 13 brings together the owners, developers, brokers, investors, and lenders shaping the future of Texas multifamily for a day of market intelligence, networking, and actionable insights. Join 300+ decision-makers and be part of the conversations driving the Texas multifamily market. Register today: www.ConnectTXMF2026.com. bullets: BH Properties acquires Tollway North Office Park (297.6K SF, 7 buildings) in Plano, Texas
BH now owns 675K+ SF across 14 buildings in Legacy Business Park; Tollway North 70% leased
AT&T HQ move to area planned 2028; thousands of jobs incoming; value-add office opportunity
stories.summary: BH Properties completed acquisition of Tollway North Office Park, a 297,591-SF seven-building business park in Plano, Texas, from KBS. The acquisition follows BH's February 2025 purchase of the adjacent R&D at Legacy campus, bringing BH's total Legacy Business Park ownership to 675,000+ SF across 14 buildings. Tollway North is currently 70% leased and presents value-add opportunities; AT&T's planned global headquarters relocation to the area is expected to bring thousands of employees beginning in 2028.
stories.impact: AT&T HQ consolidation to Plano starting 2028 signals major job inflow and talent migration to Dallas metro. Multifamily developers should acquire land and underwrite garden-style and mid-rise rentals in Plano/Legacy submarket ahead of 2027–2028 occupation; proximity to office parks and employer concentration will anchor residential demand and support rent growth. Monitor housing supply pipeline in Plano to avoid oversupply; coordinate with corporate relocation timelines.

stories.title: Teeple Adding 312-Unit Student Housing Project to Texas A&M Offering
stories.excerpt: Teeple Partners started construction on its newest apartment development, Oaks Reserve. The 312-unit community will be situated along the Innovation Corridor in the Bryan-College Station market, midway between Texas A&M University’s RELLIS Research Campus and the Texas A&M Health Science Center. Oaks Reserve is the second phase of a planned three-phase multifamily development encompassing more than 53 acres and totaling approximately 1,000 apartment homes. The first phase, Brazos Oaks (shown), consists of 315 units and was completed in June 2026. The community has experienced strong demand and is now over 90% leased. Apartment homes will have private yards with amenities that include a swimming pool, a state-of-the-art fitness facility, a conference room, a resident lounge, private workspaces and focus rooms, a package locker system, two pickleball courts and separate dog parks for small and large dogs. The community was designed by HLR Architects. Construction is being managed by Interwest Construction. Construction and permanent financing are being provided by Mason Joseph Company. The post Teeple Adding 312-Unit Student Housing Project to Texas A&M Offering appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Teeple Partners starts Oaks Reserve (312 units) in Bryan-College Station; Phase 2 of 1K-unit development
Oaks Reserve sits on Innovation Corridor between Texas A&M RELLIS and Health Science Center
Phase 1 (Brazos Oaks, 315 units) completed June 2026; now 90%+ leased; strong absorption
stories.summary: Teeple Partners began construction on Oaks Reserve, a 312-unit apartment community in Bryan-College Station positioned on the Innovation Corridor between Texas A&M University's RELLIS Research Campus and the Texas A&M Health Science Center. It is the second phase of a planned three-phase, 1,000-unit development. Phase 1 (Brazos Oaks, 315 units) completed in June 2026 and is now over 90% leased, signaling strong market demand.
stories.impact: Texas A&M market shows robust multifamily demand anchored by university and research campus expansion. Phase 1 absorption (90%+ in first few months post-delivery) validates development thesis and justifies Phase 2 start. Phased execution model works in supply-constrained college markets; monitor Phase 1 rent growth and Phase 2 lease-up to signal sustained demand. Innovation Corridor positioning (research/health sciences) attracts educated workforce and supports premium rents; replicate model in other university-anchored growth markets.

stories.title: Stonepeak Picks Up 860K-SF Rail-Served DFW Warehouse
stories.excerpt: Stonepeak acquired an 860,100-square-foot rail-served logistics asset in Fort Worth, Texas. The asset is located in the Alliance submarket of Dallas-Fort Worth, which is anchored by two Class I rail lines, the BNSF Alliance intermodal terminal, and the Fort Worth Alliance cargo airport, with direct access to the I-35 “NAFTA highway” linking Mexico to Canada. The Alliance submarket’s transport infrastructure is supported by DFW’s population of 9 million residents, which is expected to grow by 3x the national average through 2031. Stonepeak’s real estate team invests in assets that exhibit infrastructure characteristics. The team invests in supply chain, residential, healthcare and technology real estate. The team targets opportunities with high barriers to entry, inflation protection, and are mission-critical to the businesses and communities they serve. Newmark served as financial advisor to Stonepeak. The post Stonepeak Picks Up 860K-SF Rail-Served DFW Warehouse appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Stonepeak acquires 860.1K SF rail-served warehouse in DFW Alliance (Fort Worth), logistics asset
Alliance submarket: BNSF intermodal, cargo airport, I-35 access; DFW population 9M, projected 3x national growth through 2031
Infrastructure-heavy supply chain asset; no multifamily signal
stories.summary: Stonepeak acquired an 860,100-SF rail-served logistics asset in Fort Worth's Alliance submarket, which is anchored by two Class I rail lines, the BNSF Alliance intermodal terminal, Fort Worth Alliance cargo airport, and direct I-35 access. DFW's population of 9 million is expected to grow at 3x the national average through 2031. Stonepeak targets assets with high barriers to entry, inflation protection, and mission-critical supply chain characteristics.
stories.impact: DFW population growth (3x national average through 2031) is a strong multifamily demand signal; however, logistics/warehouse investment in Alliance does not directly anchor residential demand. Monitor DFW multifamily supply pipeline to ensure delivery aligns with inbound population; warehouse employment (logistics, e-commerce) typically generates lower-wage rents. Coordinate with tech and corporate office growth (e.g., AT&T Plano) to target higher-rent absorption in secondary submarkets near employment centers, not logistics hubs.
